precepts.text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. There shall come a Star out of Jacob. Out of who? Out of Jacob. Did it say out of Esau? And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: a ruler shall rise out of Israel. And shall smite the corners of Moab, the Moabites.
precepts.point: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star. So who is the morning star? Christ is the morning star. But why is it referring to Lucifer as the morning star?

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” So who is the morning star? Christ is the morning star. Then why is Lucifer called “son of the morning”? The King James is the only version with Lucifer there, because the scholars who translated it understood something everybody else did not: there is a difference between that morning star and the morning star we read about all through the scriptures.

Balaam saw the true star: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob”. A star out of who? Out of Jacob. Did it say out of Esau? No: out of Jacob.

“and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel”: a ruler shall rise out of Israel. “and shall smite the corners of Moab”, the Moabites, the Chinese, “and destroy all the children of Sheth.”

So the star in the scriptures is Christ, the ruler rising out of Israel, the offspring of David. The star comes out of Jacob, not Esau, and that is how we know the one called Lucifer, the false morning star, is a different one.

precepts.text: In the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest. What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands? It is the Son of God. That is why his king shall be higher than Agag.
precepts.point: When he looked on Amalek: that is what you call the Israelis today. Amalek was the first of the nations that fought against us, but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever. The Kenites shall be wasted until Asshur, the Assyrians, carry them away captive; Judges 1:16 tells you about the Kenites. Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber: write down 1 Maccabees 1:1 and 8:5.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Balaam, in his trance, saw that Israel’s “king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” Agag was an Edomite, a real tall one. The kingdom that is going to be exalted is the kingdom of the Lord, and the king higher than Agag is Christ.

Ezra saw that same king: “in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted”. Ezra asked the angel who these were, and he answered, “These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” Then, “What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands?” And the answer: “It is the Son of God”.

So that is what Balaam saw in the spirit realm about the Israelites. His king shall be taller even than Agag. There will be no question in the kingdom which one is the Son of God. He is going to be the tallest one, and not by an inch or a foot; it is going to be astronomically clear. You will look and say, that is the Son of God right there.

And Balaam saw more of him: “he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows.” Balaam saw Christ destroying the nations. And “Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee”: anybody that blesses Israel shall be blessed, and anybody that curses us shall be cursed.

precepts.text: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. God got tired of him and had him put to death.
precepts.point: When he looked on Amalek: that is what you call the Israelis today. Amalek was the first of the nations that fought against us, but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever. The Kenites shall be wasted until Asshur, the Assyrians, carry them away captive; Judges 1:16 tells you about the Kenites. Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber: write down 1 Maccabees 1:1 and 8:5.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Balaam dealt with enchantments, which lets us know he was a witch, a soothsayer, a diviner. When it says “the spirit of God came upon him”, notice the little s: this is on the left hand side. It is not the Holy Spirit coming on Balaam. He would fall into trances with his eyes wide open and see visions, and he knew it was the Lord sending that spirit upon him, which is why he told Balak he could not go beyond the commandment of the Lord. Even so, he saw Christ only from afar: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh”, because he is not an Israelite.

What happened to Balaam? “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” What was he? The soothsayer: a witch, a warlock.

The Lord had used that witch, sending unrighteous angels to tell him this and tell him that. Then he told the Israelites: kill Balaam, destroy him; he is not our people. God got tired of him and had him put to death.

That is the end of the false prophet. Balaam could see all the way to the latter days and speak blessings over Israel, but his gift came from the left hand side, and he was slain among the enemies of Israel.

precepts.text: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

precepts.text: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, as trees which the Lord hath planted.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Balaam, “the man whose eyes are open”, saw the vision of the Almighty and said: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.”

People think these tabernacles are houses. They are our bodies. It is us being that tree by the river, planted by the Lord, beside the living waters. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters”: the waters are poured out from on high, from the Lord, and we will be swimming in those living waters, the waters from heaven above the firmament, not space. “and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” The king is Christ, and that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things were brought out to encourage us. They have been hidden for thousands of years, and understanding them builds up our hope.

precepts.text: A Star out of Jacob and a Sceptre out of Israel; Edom shall be a possession, and Israel shall do valiantly.
precepts.point: In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

note.label: Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac

precepts.why:
Balaam saw it: “there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly.”

Edom a possession, and Israel doing valiantly: that is the seed possessing the gate of his enemies, sworn to Abraham by the Lord Himself. The covenant has Israel possessing their enemies, and Edom is named. All nations cannot be inside a covenant like that; the nations blessed in Abraham’s seed are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: I raised up of your sons for prophets; the prophets come out of the children of Israel, not the nations.
precepts.point: That does not make the other nations prophets. Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel; the Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose, to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him.” Do not be confused at the spirit of God coming on a man of another nation: all the spirits belong to the Most High, and He can do what He wants with any of them.

That does not make the other nations prophets. “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.” Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel, not the nations.

The Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose: to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

precepts.text: Sanctified and cleansed with the washing of water by the word; the water is the word.
precepts.point: His seed shall be in many waters means Israel scattered all over the earth, and his kingdom shall be exalted higher than Agag.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters.” The water is the word. Christ loved the church “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

The washing of water by the word is how the church is sanctified and cleansed, and that is how you cleanse your spirit. The water poured out of his buckets is the word, and his seed in many waters is Israel scattered all over the earth, with his kingdom exalted higher than Agag.

precepts.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? By taking heed thereto according to thy word.
precepts.point: His seed shall be in many waters means Israel scattered all over the earth, and his kingdom shall be exalted higher than Agag.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The water poured out of his buckets is the word. “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

A young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word, as the church is cleansed with the washing of water by the word. That is how you cleanse your spirit: the water is the word, and his seed in many waters is Israel scattered all over the earth.

precepts.text: The cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things choke the word; those are the promotions Satan offers.
precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
Balak said, “I thought to promote thee unto great honour; but, lo, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour.” That was Satan speaking through Balak, trying to entice Balaam with honor to curse Israel.

Satan promotes with honor, riches, prestige, and lust. “And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things are the promotions Satan offers, and they choke the word.

Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up. Resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

precepts.text: When they have heard, Satan cometh immediately and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The honor Balak offered was Satan's device against a man who had just spoken the word of the Lord. “And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.”

When the word is sown, Satan comes immediately to take it away, using whatever device fits where you are: honor for Balaam, riches, prestige, or lust for another. He is an old spirit using the same tricks from the beginning of time.

precepts.text: The devil offered Christ all the power and glory of the kingdoms for worship; the same spirit offered Balaam honor through Balak.
precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The same spirit that offered Balaam honor through Balak tried the same device on Christ. “And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

All the power and the glory of the kingdoms in exchange for worship, as great honour was offered Balaam in exchange for cursing Israel. “And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.”

Satan is an old spirit using the same tricks from the beginning of time: promotion by honor, riches, prestige, and lust.

precepts.text: Balaam the son of Beor was slain with the sword beside the five kings of Midian; the Midianites were his people.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“And now, behold, I go unto my people.” Who were Balaam's people? The Midianites. When Israel went against Midian, “they slew the kings of Midian, beside the rest of them that were slain; namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.”

Balaam died with the sword beside the five kings of Midian; that is the people he went unto.

precepts.text: God hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son; the last days began at Christ.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.” The latter days are the last days, and the last days began when Christ came on the earth, was crucified, and resurrected.

“God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.” In these last days He has spoken by His Son; the last days began at Christ.

So what Balaam advertised of the latter days is what Israel shall do to the nations from the time of Christ onward.

precepts.text: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The latter days began at Christ, and the Lord's days are not ours. “But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; that is the measure of the last days Balaam spoke of. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

precepts.text: He hath torn, and he will heal us; after two days will he revive us, and in the third day raise us up.
precepts.point: A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
With a day as a thousand years to the Lord, Hosea gives the days of the latter days. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.”

He hath torn, and He will heal us; after two days He will revive us, and in the third day raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

precepts.text: Job shall see his redeemer for himself and his eyes shall behold him; Balaam shall behold him, but not nigh.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh.” Balaam is saying the Most High will raise him up again in the last days, but as a servant, far off from the King; he will behold him, but he will not be near him.

Compare that with Job. “For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.”

Job shall see his redeemer for himself and his own eyes shall behold Him; Balaam shall behold Him, but not nigh. The contrast shows Job was an Israelite and not of another nation. Balaam has no such nearness, because the redeemer is not his.

precepts.text: I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star; the Star out of Jacob is Christ.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“there shall come a Star out of Jacob”: the Star is Christ. “I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.”

Christ is the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star, and He came out of Jacob. That is the Star Balaam saw in the latter days, but not nigh.

precepts.text: The word to them that hold thrones is addressed to kings; the sceptre speaks of a king.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel.” To whom does the sceptre belong? Wisdom's word on thrones and sceptres is addressed to kings: “Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations.”

The sceptre speaks of a king, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

precepts.text: Thrones and sceptres belong to kings; the Sceptre rising out of Israel is Christ the King.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore.” Thrones and sceptres belong to kings.

So “a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel” is the King rising out of Israel: Christ the King, the same Star out of Jacob.

precepts.text: Asia has made herself like Babylon, which is America; her plagues come, and her glory dries up as a flower when the heat arises.
precepts.point: The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The Sceptre out of Israel “shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.” Balaam is prophesying of the latter days. Moab is the Chinese and Ammon the Japanese, and Sheth goes into the Egyptian. Asia is partaker of the hope of Babylon, going through the earth buying up land, trying to become financially what America already is and to deal with all nations as she has.

“And thou, Asia, that art partaker of the hope of Babylon, and art the glory of her person: Woe be unto thee, thou wretch, because thou hast made thyself like unto her.” Babylon is America, and Asia has made herself like her, decking her daughters in whoredom and following “her that is hated in all her works and inventions.”

The judgment on her is written: “therefore saith God, I will send plagues upon thee; widowhood, poverty, famine, sword, and pestilence, to waste thy houses with destruction and death. And the glory of thy Power shall be dried up as a flower, the heat shall arise that is sent over thee.” Plagues, widowhood, poverty, famine, sword, and pestilence, and the glory of her power dried up as a flower when the heat arises that is sent over her: that is the smiting of the corners of Moab.

precepts.text: Woe unto Babylon, Asia, Egypt, and Syria; destruction is coming on them all.
precepts.point: The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The Sceptre out of Israel smites the corners of Moab and destroys all the children of Sheth: Moab the Chinese, Ammon the Japanese, and Sheth going into the Egyptian. Esdras names them together: “Woe be unto thee, Babylon, and Asia! woe be unto thee, Egypt and Syria!”

Woe unto Babylon, Asia, Egypt, and Syria; destruction is coming on them all in the latter days Balaam saw.

precepts.text: For the reproach of Moab and the revilings of Ammon, Moab shall be as Sodom and Ammon as Gomorrah, the remnant of the Most High's people shall possess them, and men shall worship the Lord every one from his place.
precepts.point: The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
Balaam saw the Sceptre out of Israel smite the corners of Moab, and Zephaniah gives the judgment. “I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border.”

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation.” Moab shall be as Sodom and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, the breeding of nettles and salt pits; the stinging nettle is a plant that burns, and the fire that fell on Sodom is coming again.

“the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.” The residue of the Most High's people, the third that is left, shall spoil them, and the remnant shall possess them, for their pride against the people of the Lord of hosts.

“The Lord will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen.” That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

precepts.text: The heathen round about are bought for bondmen and taken for a possession for ever; that is what Edom becomes to Israel.
precepts.point: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly.” Edom is nowhere named in the matter of Balak and Balaam in these chapters, but the Lord made sure Edom was written into the prophecy. The law of bondmen shows what a possession is.

“Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.” Of the strangers that sojourn among you and their families, “they shall be your possession. And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.”

The heathen round about are bought for an inheritance, bondmen for ever, though over our own brethren we do not rule with rigour. That is what Edom becomes to Israel: a possession. But for Esau that servitude is not for ever, because Esau is the only nation on the earth with an expiration date; the rest of the nations go into servitude for ever, but the Lord can only bear with Esau so much longer.

precepts.text: The house of Jacob shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.
precepts.point: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
Edom shall be a possession, but for Esau that servitude is not for ever, because Esau is the only nation on the earth with an expiration date.

“And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” The house of Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel, the blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, shall be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble.

There shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. The rest of the nations go into servitude for ever, but the Lord can only bear with Esau so much longer; that is Israel doing valiantly.

precepts.text: He that cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah treads the winepress in his fury, for the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come.
precepts.point: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy him that remaineth of the city.” That is the one who cometh from Edom. “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” The greatness of his strength is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.”

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end. He that has dominion out of Jacob destroys him that remaineth, and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.

precepts.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim; that is why Amalek is called the first of the nations.
precepts.point: His latter end shall be that he perish for ever; precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“Amalek was the first of the nations.” That means Amalek was the first of the nations to come out and fight against Israel: “Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.”

He met us at Rephidim as we came out of Egypt, before any other nation lifted a hand against Israel; that is why Amalek is called the first of the nations.

precepts.text: The remembrance of Amalek shall be utterly put out from under heaven, for the Lord hath sworn to have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
precepts.point: His latter end shall be that he perish for ever; precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.” The Lord swore it at Rephidim: “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.” Moses built an altar and called it JEHOVAH-nissi, “Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

Amalek is the seed of Esau through Eliphaz, and Amalek is the people who call themselves Jewish in the land of Israel today. The war that has never left that land since they entered it is the war the Lord swore to have with Amalek from generation to generation, and the prophecy that none shall remain of the house of Esau belongs to no other nation.

Precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is: the remembrance of him utterly put out from under heaven, perishing for ever.

precepts.text: Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim and afflict Asshur and Eber, tying together with the ships of Chittim that come against him.
precepts.point: He returns and has intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time.

note.label: Daniel 11: The Kings of the North and the South

precepts.why:
“And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.” This ties together with the ships of Chittim that come against him here: ships from the coast of Chittim, afflicting Asshur and Eber.

So when he returns toward the south at the time appointed, it is not as the former, because the ships of Chittim come against him. He is grieved and has indignation against the holy covenant, and has intelligence with them that forsake it, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time.

precepts.text: There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Balaam saw him afar off: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.”

The Star out of Jacob and the Sceptre rising out of Israel is Christ, written in the law of Moses. He came to fulfil what was said of him there.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 18: Babylon Is Fallen

precepts.why:
“He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up?”: he compares the whole twelve tribes of Israel to a lion. “Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.” Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, so are those nations blessed or cursed? They are all cursed.

The ones in power know what happened to us; you don’t lead a nation and be dumb. Like the king in Esther who could not sleep and read the chronicles of Persia, they have records of everything. The president of Iran stood at the UN and spoke of the tens of millions abducted from Africa and other regions of the world, and asked why reparations are paid for the Holocaust but not to the nations affected by slavery, and the European delegates walked out. They know the history, but they will only go so far; they will never tell us who we are, because it disrupts their plans of power.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Amalek was the first of the nations, the first to attack us out of Egypt, and his latter end is to perish for ever: condemned at the very beginning of the Bible, and there is no saving this family.

They attacked from behind, where the elders, the mothers and the children were, cowards then and now, dropping bombs and running off, crying about antisemitism because they are not built for war though they are murderous and very emotional.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

Come, and I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh. Balaam the witch revealed to the king, I am going to see Christ in the last days, but not near, because he is not an Israelite, but he will witness what is going on. There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: this is Christ, the star of Jacob, the king that shall rise out of Israel.

He shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth: anybody that worships the Egyptian god Seth. And Edom shall be a possession: Edom shall become servants to this people, and Israel shall do valiantly.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: When he looked on Amalek: that is what you call the Israelis today. Amalek was the first of the nations that fought against us, but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever. The Kenites shall be wasted until Asshur, the Assyrians, carry them away captive; Judges 1:16 tells you about the Kenites. Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber: write down 1 Maccabees 1:1 and 8:5.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he went not to seek enchantments, and the spirit of God came upon him. Do not be confused at the spirit of God coming on a man of another nation: all the spirits belong to the Most High, and He can do what He wants with any of them.

That does not make the other nations prophets. Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel; the Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose, to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Balaam heard the words of God and saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open. Picture a man staring off as if daydreaming: he is seeing visions with his eyes open while the Lord gives him what to say to the nations that are trying to do evil to Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters. The water is the word: Christ sanctifies and cleanses the church with the washing of water by the word, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word. That is how you cleanse your spirit.
His seed shall be in many waters means Israel scattered all over the earth, and his kingdom shall be exalted higher than Agag.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: God brought him forth out of Egypt with as it were the strength of an unicorn; he shall eat up the nations his enemies, break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows. That is the destruction coming on Israel's enemies when we rise back up.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: He couched, he lay down as a great lion, and who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee. Balaam is speaking the very prophecies and promises that belong to Israel throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

I will advertise thee what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days. The latter days are the last days, and the last days began when Christ came on the earth, was crucified, and resurrected: God, who spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by His Son.

A thousand years is as a day to the Lord, and a day as a thousand years; as Hosea says, after two days He will revive us, and in the third day He will raise us up. The full teaching of that timing belongs to another class.

Compare that with Job, and the contrast shows Job was an Israelite and not of another nation: Job knew that his redeemer liveth, that in his flesh he shall see God, whom he shall see for himself and his eyes shall behold, and not another. Balaam has no such nearness, because the redeemer is not his.

There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

And shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. Balaam is prophesying of the latter days: this teaching identifies Moab with the Chinese and Ammon with the Japanese, and Sheth goes into the Egyptian. Asia is partaker of the hope of Babylon, going through the earth buying up land, trying to become financially what America already is and to deal with all nations as she has.

The judgment on her is written: plagues, widowhood, poverty, famine, sword, and pestilence, and the glory of her power dried up as a flower when the heat arises that is sent over her. Moab shall be as Sodom and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, the breeding of nettles and salt pits; the stinging nettle is a plant that burns, and the fire that fell on Sodom is coming again.
The residue of the Most High's people, the third that is left, shall spoil them, and the remnant shall possess them; this shall they have for their pride against the people of the Lord of hosts.

The Lord will be terrible unto them and famish all the gods of the earth, and men shall worship Him every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. That is why Balaam said he shall behold Him, but not nigh: the nations will worship from their own place and come up only at the appointed times of the year.

points: The Kenite's dwelling place was strong, his nest put in a rock; nevertheless the Kenite shall be wasted and go into captivity, until Asshur, which is the Assyrians, shall carry him away captive.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Alas, who shall live when God doeth this! Ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and Chittim is Italy; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever. Eber here is not speaking of Israel, for other peoples besides us came out of Eber, who is of Shem; the history of prophecy opens this up as the prophets are read.
